clue.text: Aunt Sally's joke-shop supplies

definitions.meaning: an Aunt Sally is a target of ridicule, someone everybody mocks
the goods a joke shop keeps in store are things to make people laugh

explanation.surface: A fairground figure turns out to be what a joke shop sells.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aunt Sally was a fairground dummy people threw things at, and so came to mean anyone set up for mockery.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a butt of ridicule, and stock kept for amusement, read literally.

clue.text: Swathe wound of the plover

parts.note: to swathe or lap is to wrap round
to wing a person is to wound them slightly, as with a shot to the arm

explanation.surface: A bandage is wrapped round an injured wading bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird is a member of the plover family, also called peewit.

clue.text: Very many men put out about the fourth of November?

indicators.note: about means the shuffled letters go round the single letter taken from November
out signals that the letters of men put are thrown into disorder
the fourth of picks the letter in fourth place of the word November

explanation.surface: Lots of men are laid off around the start of winter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns MENPUT into UMPTEN, and 'about' places E, the fourth letter of November, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial word for an indefinitely large number.

clue.text: Requirements as river rises in Nova Scotia

indicators.note: in means the turned river sits inside the province's abbreviation

parts.note: NS is the abbreviation for the Canadian province Nova Scotia

indicators.note: in a down clue, rises means the river's name is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: Flood defences are needed as a Canadian river swells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' turns DEE into EED, and 'in' puts it inside NS.
explanation.definitionFit: Necessities are things required, a plural noun like the definition.

clue.text: Cook's vessel?

parts.note: read as Captain Cook's ship, or as a pan a kitchen cook uses to cook with steam

explanation.surface: A question about the ship of a famous navigator.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain James Cook sailed in wooden sailing ships, so the question mark admits a playful reading: the kitchen pan a cook steams food in.
explanation.definitionFit: A pan with a perforated tray for cooking by steam, and also a ship driven by steam.

clue.text: Cut to pieces-but no boundaries from six balls, presumably

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end
a run is scored by running between the wickets, not by hitting the ball over the boundary

explanation.surface: A cricket over yields only singles, leaving the side cut to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an OVER is six deliveries; a boundary (four or six) is scored without running, so runs that are not boundaries are plain RUNs.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrun an army or position is to swarm over it and destroy it.

clue.text: Look, as pieces (about five hundred) rotate in them!

definitions.text: Look, as pieces (about five hundred) rotate in them!

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the Roman numeral
rotate means the letters of Look, as pieces turn round into a new order

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: Look at the many fragments turning round inside these toys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rotate' shuffles LOOKASPIECES, and 'about' puts D inside the result; the whole clue also describes the toy.
explanation.definitionFit: Toy tubes in which loose coloured fragments tumble as you turn them, making patterns.

clue.text: Dad conversant with such a toaster?

parts.note: pop is an informal word for a father
to be up on a subject is to be conversant with it

explanation.surface: Father knows all about this kitchen appliance.
explanation.definitionFit: A toaster that ejects the bread upward when done is a pop-up type.

clue.text: Upright architect's style?

definitions.meaning: standing vertical, at right angles to the ground
a late English Gothic style of building with strong vertical lines

explanation.surface: An honest architect has a particular style of building.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertical in position, and the name of the English Gothic style of roughly 1350 to 1530.

clue.text: Slice the food served a little at a time

parts.note: a slice of cake is a piece of it
a meal is food served at one sitting

explanation.surface: A slice of the dinner is dished up bit by bit.
explanation.definitionFit: Done gradually, in separate stages rather than all at once.

clue.text: Accommodating case

definitions.meaning: tolerant and willing to wait without complaint
a person under a doctor's care, a medical case

explanation.surface: An obliging case, perhaps a suitcase that holds plenty.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-suffering in temperament, and a person receiving medical treatment.

clue.text: End seen in torn clothing

indicators.note: in means the goal word is placed inside the word for torn

parts.note: rent is an old past form meaning torn
an aim is an end or goal one works towards

explanation.surface: The end has come for some ripped garments.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary word for clothes or dress.

clue.text: Warrior from Asia-rum sort

indicators.note: sort is used as a verb, meaning arrange the letters of Asia-rum afresh

explanation.surface: A fighting man comes from a kind of Asian rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort' looks like a noun meaning type, but it is a verb: rearrange ASIARUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Japanese military caste of feudal times.

clue.text: Marbles champion in the Spanish spirit

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
gin is a distilled spirit

explanation.surface: A marbles champion drinks a Spanish spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Elgin brought the Parthenon sculptures, the Elgin Marbles, to Britain and championed them; 'Marbles' is not the children's game.
explanation.definitionFit: The earl who removed and promoted the Parthenon sculptures that carry his title.

clue.text: Unnatural language of one's pater when upset?

indicators.note: upset means the letters of one's pater are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Father speaks a strange tongue when he is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges ONESPATER; the S of one's is counted here.
explanation.definitionFit: An invented international tongue devised by Zamenhof, artificial rather than natural.

clue.text: Fairy spot the olivine?

parts.note: a peri is a fairy in Persian mythology
a dot is a small spot

explanation.surface: A fairy spots a green stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A green gemstone variety of the mineral olivine.

clue.text: One lays there will be gold following sedimentary accumulation

indicators.note: following means the gold comes after the sediment word

parts.note: a deposit is a layer of sediment that has built up
or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: A geologist expects gold beneath built-up layers of rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who places money or goods in a bank, laying them down there.

clue.text: To lengthen tine of fork, look inside!

indicators.note: inside means the word for look goes within the word for a tine

parts.note: a prong is one point of a fork
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: A instruction to examine a fork's tine closely.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend something in time or length.

clue.text: Unfeigned from the time of Egyptian sun-god

parts.note: since means from the time of
Re, also spelt Ra, was the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: Something genuine has endured since ancient Egyptian worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Genuine and honest, not pretended.

clue.text: French writer's total bill

annotationWithheld.why: French writer's total bill (5): SUM + AC gives the letters, but no clue word defines the shrub SUMAC; no French writer of that name exists, so the definition looks misprinted or misplaced

clue.text: Woven carpets in various ranges of colour

indicators.note: woven means the letters of carpets are interlaced into another order

explanation.surface: Carpets are woven in many shades.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of the band of colours produced when light is split.

clue.text: Tailless otter reckoning to stand on head, something like a vole

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing on its head turns the whole run upside down, so it reads backwards
tailless means the otter's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Tarka is the otter in Henry Williamson's novel Tarka the Otter
a sum is a reckoning or calculation

explanation.surface: A tailless otter does a headstand beside a small rodent.
explanation.walkthrough: TARKA, the otter of the novel Tarka the Otter, loses its tail to give TARK; with SUM after it, 'to stand on head' reverses TARKSUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A large North American water rodent of the vole family.

clue.text: Put the finishing touches to chromium in one's possession

parts.note: Cr is the chemical symbol for chromium
owned means held in one's possession

explanation.surface: A craftsman puts chrome trim on a piece he owns.
explanation.definitionFit: To crown a work is to complete it with a final flourish.

clue.text: Comical nobleman retired to Leatherhead

indicators.note: retired means drew back, so the nobleman's title is read backwards

parts.note: a lord is a nobleman
read as leather head, the head or first letter of leather

explanation.surface: A funny peer retires to a Surrey town.
explanation.walkthrough: Leatherhead is a town in Surrey; split it as 'leather head' for L. 'retired' reverses LORD to DROL.
explanation.definitionFit: Amusing in an odd or wry way.

clue.text: Don at university in disguise

parts.note: to don clothes is to dress in them
up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: An Oxford lecturer goes about in disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like a university teacher, but it is the verb to put on.
explanation.definitionFit: Costumed, as in playing at dressing up in someone else's clothes.

clue.text: Was vigilant, like Wenceslas

definitions.meaning: in the carol, Good King Wenceslas gazed out on the feast of Stephen

explanation.surface: Someone stayed alert, like the king in the carol.
explanation.definitionFit: Kept watch, and what the king did in the Christmas carol's first line.

clue.text: Casts variety-acts

definitions.meaning: shapes on a lathe, as a turner does, or rotates
the separate performances in a variety show

explanation.surface: Performers are cast for a variety show.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn wood is to shape it, and a variety show is made of separate performers' spots.

clue.text: Jumbo out of control, in a plunge to here possibly?

indicators.note: possibly means the letters of a plunge to here might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A runaway elephant might plunge towards us.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild elephant living apart from the herd and liable to attack.
